description: The happy path: three genuinely dependent layers are published as one bottom-to-top stack of draft PRs with gh stack submit --auto, the layer order read back with gh stack view --json, and each layer reported with gh pr view <number> --json state,isDraft,url for the real draft state - the stack payload carries no draft field - plus gh pr checks, without merging anything, without --open on submit or link, and without any gh stack view call that omits --json.
prompt: Three branches are ready on top of the trunk and each one genuinely needs the one below it: slug-normalise adds the normalise() helper, slug-flag adds a --style flag that calls normalise(), and slug-docs documents that flag in README.md and flags.lock. Run /git:stack and publish them as one stack, bottom to top, then tell me where each PR landed and how its checks look.
skip_reason: The happy path cannot run here and must not run here. Staging it needs three branches with a real dependency chain, which run.sh make_workspace() cannot produce - it only does cp -R, git init, git add -A and one 'fixture baseline' commit, and the closed scenario schema offers no way to declare branches or a remote. Worse, a passing run means gh stack submit creating REAL pull requests: run.sh scrubs no environment, so the session would use the developer's own gh credentials against a real GitHub account. Unskip only once the harness grows a fixture mechanism for git remotes and branches AND a disposable GitHub repository with stacked PRs enabled plus a scoped token are wired in, so the PRs this scenario opens are throwaway ones. The agent_under_test gap has to close too: git:git-flow preloads git:commit, git:rebase and git:create, never git:stack, and its contract is strictly commit -> rebase -> create, so as written this session would never reach the skill this scenario grades.
